subject: implicit type checks & error messages for multivar normal

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: implicit type checks & error messages for multivar normal
parts:
I'm looking at distributions_multi_normal and had
a bunch of thoughts.

0. We only need to use our matrix functions if
we don't know what the types are. Once we know
what the types are for the propto overrides,
we can use the built-ins like .transpose() which
are much faster (e.g., no intermediate memory
and no copying in the case of transpose()). We'll
know where we need to promote.

1. We probably want to have a parameterization
in terms of Sigma_inverse. Inverting the matrix
every time is going to be expensive.
det(inv(Sigma)) = 1/det(Sigma), so that's no problem.

2. We need more checks on dimensionality. For instance,
we need y.size() == mu.size() == Sigma.rows() == Sigma.cols().

3. For the errors, the same char* function doesn't make
sense. If I understand properly, the value y
will get substituted into function, but that's not right,
as we don't want multi_normal_log<y>(y) to come out.

4. Some of the checks we can probably drop as they'll raise
the right errors through eigen. For instance, checking the
covariance matrix is positive definite happens implicitly
as part of determinant anyway. We probably do want to check
symmetry if that's not implied.

- Bob
